json.title: [PostgreSQL] pgoutput streaming decoder binds tuple values to the wrong columns after any snapshot schema refresh when the publication has a column list
json.body:
## Bug report

With `plugin.name=pgoutput` and a publication created with a per-table **column list**
(`CREATE PUBLICATION p FOR TABLE t (col_a, col_b, ...)`), the first streamed change after
**any** snapshot decodes every tuple value against the wrong column.

If the mis-bound types are incompatible the connector stops with e.g.
`Cannot parse time/date value '3.00', expected format 'y..y-MM-dd HH:mm:ss[.S]X'`.
If they happen to be compatible, **nothing is raised and wrong values are emitted** — a
publication column list can *reorder* as well as subset, so this is a silent-corruption bug
as much as a crash. A connector restart clears it (a new replication session re-sends
RELATION messages); it recurs on the next snapshot.

---

**What Debezium connector do you use and what version?**

`postgresql-connector`, **3.6.0.Final** (run as Debezium Server, `quay.io/debezium/server:3.6.0.Final`, stock image, pristine connector jar).

Verified present unchanged in `v3.6.1.Final` (`PostgresSchema.java`, `PgOutputMessageDecoder.java` and `PostgresSnapshotChangeEventSource.java` are byte-identical to `v3.6.0.Final`) and on `main` — `PostgresSchema.java:91` still reads
`connection.readSchema(tables(), null, null, getTableFilter(), null, true)`.

---

**What is the connector configuration?**

The relevant properties (the rest is transport):

```properties
connector.class=io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector
plugin.name=pgoutput
publication.name=p
publication.autocreate.mode=disabled
snapshot.mode=no_data
signal.enabled.channels=source
topic.prefix=repro
```

---

**What is the captured database version and mode of deployment?**

PostgreSQL 18, local Docker (Debezium Server standalone against a containerised Postgres). Nothing cloud-specific — the defect is purely in the decoder/schema-registry interaction.

---

**What behavior do you expect?**

When the publication publishes a subset (or a reordering) of a table's columns, the streaming
decoder should keep binding tuple values against the column list the RELATION message
described, across snapshots.

---

**What behavior do you see?**

The i-th **published** value is decoded as the i-th **physical** column of the table, from the
first streamed change after a snapshot until the replication session is re-established.

### Why

1. `PgOutputMessageDecoder.handleRelationMessage` (lines 410-411) builds a `Table` from the
   pgoutput RELATION message — i.e. the **publication's** column list — and stores it in the
   shared schema registry via `PostgresSchema.applySchemaChangesForTable(relationId, table)`.
2. `PostgresSchema.refresh(PostgresConnection, boolean)` **line 91** then re-reads every
   captured table over JDBC:
   `connection.readSchema(tables(), null, null, getTableFilter(), null, true)`.
   The 5th argument is the **column filter** and it is hard-coded `null`;
   `JdbcConnection.readTableColumn` (line 1394) treats `null` as "keep everything", so the
   registry entry is overwritten with **every physical column** of the table. The
   relation-derived model is gone.
3. `PgOutputMessageDecoder.resolveRelation` (line 676) → `resolveColumnsFromStreamTupleData`
   (**line 763**) binds the tuple **positionally** against whatever the registry now holds:
   `final io.debezium.relational.Column column = table.columns().get(i);`

Postgres does not re-send a RELATION message merely because the connector re-read
`pg_attribute`, so nothing repairs the binding until the replication session is re-established.

**Both snapshot paths reach step 2:**

* blocking — `PostgresSnapshotChangeEventSource.readTableStructure` (lines 227-235):
  `readSchema(..., null, false)` then `schema.refresh(jdbcConnection, false)`;
* incremental — `PostgresSignalBasedIncrementalSnapshotChangeEventSource.refreshTableSchema`
  → `PostgresSchema.refreshFromIncrementalSnapshot` (line 173) →
  `PostgresSchema.refresh(connection, tableId, …)` (line 125), `null` column filter again.

Two notes that make this wider than it looks:

* An incremental snapshot that exports **zero rows** still poisons the binding —
  `refreshTableSchema` runs before the max-key query.
* Narrowing a signal's `data-collections` does not contain the blast radius:
  `schema.refresh()` re-reads **every** table matching `getTableFilter()`, so a one-table
  snapshot mis-binds all captured tables.

`refreshFromIncrementalSnapshot` already carries the **DBZ-8150** fix, which strips GENERATED
columns during the incremental refresh — the same mechanism with a different trigger. Columns
missing because the publication simply does not publish them were never covered, and nothing in
Debezium reads `pg_publication_tables.attnames`.

Not reachable by configuration, as far as I can tell: `schema.refresh.mode` governs only
whether missing TOASTable data suppresses a refresh
(`skipRefreshSchemaOnMissingToastableData`) and never touches the decoder's binding;
`snapshot.mode.configuration.based.snapshot.schema` does not help because
`RelationalSnapshotChangeEventSource` calls `readTableStructure` unconditionally; and
`publication.autocreate.mode=filtered` "fixes" it only by rewriting the publication without
column lists.

---

**How to reproduce**

Deterministic, 3 steps.

```sql
CREATE TABLE public.orders (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id uuid NOT NULL, software_version varchar,
  order_number varchar, customer_id uuid, store_id uuid, status varchar,
  delivery_date timestamptz, total_amount numeric(12,2), tip numeric(12,2));
ALTER TABLE public.orders REPLICA IDENTITY FULL;
CREATE PUBLICATION p FOR TABLE public.orders
  (id, tenant_id, customer_id, store_id, status, delivery_date, total_amount, tip);
```

The published list's 8th column is `tip` (`numeric`); the table's 8th physical column is
`delivery_date` (`timestamptz`):

```
WAL position (publication column list)      table ordinal (all physical columns)
 1 id                                        1 id                     ok
 2 tenant_id                                 2 tenant_id              ok
 3 customer_id                               3 software_version
 4 store_id                                  4 order_number
 5 status                                    5 customer_id
 6 delivery_date                             6 store_id
 7 total_amount                              7 status
 8 tip           '3.00'  ────────────────►   8 delivery_date  timestamptz   <-- parse failure
```

With the connector configuration above:

1. Start the connector and `INSERT` a row — it decodes correctly.
2. Send an `execute-snapshot` signal, `"type":"blocking"` **or** `"type":"incremental"`.
3. `INSERT` another row →
   `ERROR Cannot parse time/date value '3.00', expected format 'y..y-MM-dd HH:mm:ss[.S]X'`
   and the connector stops.

Measured on the stock `quay.io/debezium/server:3.6.0.Final` image, each round restarting the
connector, writing a control row, running a full snapshot, then writing a row:

| Publication shape | Rounds survived |
|---|---|
| column list | **0 / 5** — every round fails as above |
| column list + the patch below | **5 / 5**, payload fields asserted correct, exactly the published columns present |
| no column list (full row) | **5 / 5** |

Change one type in the table so the shifted values stay parseable and the same rounds emit
**wrong values with no error at all**, which is the case I would flag as the real severity.

---

**Do you see the same behaviour using the latest released Debezium version?**

Yes. `v3.6.1.Final` is byte-identical in the three files involved, and `main` still has the
hard-coded `null` column filter at `PostgresSchema.java:91`.

---

**Suggested fix (validated patch, inline — not submitting a PR)**

Decode against the structure the **stream** described, rather than whatever the shared schema
registry currently holds. A decoder-local map of relation-derived tables is correct regardless
of *why* the two lists differ, which the narrow DBZ-8150 fix is not. This is essentially the
shape SQL Server already settled on in DBZ-2495 / DBZ-2522 (table model derived from the
capture instance's column list).

```diff
--- a/debezium-connector-postgres/src/main/java/io/debezium/connector/postgresql/connection/pgoutput/PgOutputMessageDecoder.java
+++ b/debezium-connector-postgres/src/main/java/io/debezium/connector/postgresql/connection/pgoutput/PgOutputMessageDecoder.java
@@
 import java.util.Collections;
+import java.util.HashMap;
 import java.util.HashSet;
@@
     private final MessageDecoderContext decoderContext;
     private final PostgresConnection connection;
 
+    /**
+     * The table structure of each relation AS THE STREAM DESCRIBES IT, keyed by relation id.
+     * Tuple data is positional against the most recent relation message's column list; the
+     * schema registry is re-read from JDBC without a column filter by paths unrelated to
+     * decoding, after which it carries every column of the table.
+     */
+    private final Map<Integer, Table> relationTables = new HashMap<>();
+
     private Instant commitTimestamp;
@@ handleRelationMessage
         Table table = resolveRelationFromMetadata(new PgOutputRelationMetaData(relationId, schemaName, tableName, columns, primaryKeyColumns));
         decoderContext.getSchema().applySchemaChangesForTable(relationId, table);
+        if (decoderContext.getSchema().tableFor(relationId) != null) {
+            relationTables.put(relationId, table);
+        }
     }
@@ resolveRelation
     private Optional<Table> resolveRelation(int relationId) {
+        final Table relationTable = relationTables.get(relationId);
+        if (relationTable != null) {
+            return Optional.of(relationTable);
+        }
         return Optional.ofNullable(decoderContext.getSchema().tableFor(relationId));
     }
```

A narrower alternative — passing `connectorConfig.getColumnFilter()` instead of `null` at
`PostgresSchema.java:91` and `:125` — repairs the case where `column.include.list` happens to
match the publication, but not a publication column list on its own, which is exactly the
configuration with no other enforcement.

How the patch was validated without a Maven build (the server image ships a full JDK, so the
single file compiles against the jars already present and the class can be swapped into the
connector jar):

```bash
docker cp PgOutputMessageDecoder.java debezium:/tmp/
docker exec debezium sh -lc '
  CP=$(ls /debezium/lib/*.jar | tr "\n" ":")
  /usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk/bin/javac -nowarn -proc:none -cp "$CP" -d /tmp/out /tmp/PgOutputMessageDecoder.java
  cd /tmp/out && /usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk/bin/jar uf \
    /debezium/lib/debezium-connector-postgres-3.6.0.Final.jar \
    $(find io -name "PgOutputMessageDecoder*.class")'
docker restart debezium
```

Happy to rework this into a PR with a test if the approach looks right — filing the report
first since the fix touches the decoder's relationship with the shared schema registry and a
maintainer may prefer a different placement.

---

**Related**

* **DBZ-8150** — same mechanism, GENERATED-columns trigger, fixed narrowly inside
  `refreshFromIncrementalSnapshot`.
* **DBZ-2495 / DBZ-2522** — SQL Server derived its table model from the capture instance's
  column list; that is the shape this needs.
* debezium/dbz#2020 — open sibling report (incremental snapshot, generated column).

Hi @arjunQDC, thanks for the report. 

The concern I have with allowing the publication to dictate the columns here is that if the column include/exclude list does not directly align with the publication definition, then won't you end up with potentially where columns are emitted as null, or worse, failures because a field may be defined as not-null in the relational model, yet no value is being published because the publication excluded it.

Right now, when we auto-manage the publication, we don't push column include/exclude rules, so that would likely need to be another area added to guarantee we aren't putting the ownership of dual management on the user.

@arjunQDC We'd be glad to get a PR! Also I'd recommend to introduce at least in the beginning a check that would ensure that either column filtering is set at connector level or at publication level but not in both - in that case connector would fail.

> and i dont think users should have to keep column.include.list in sync with the publication at all. postgres already knows what the publication covers.
> ...
> auto managed publications shouldnt be affected since debezium never creates them with column lists anyway. the divergence can only happen when someone hand manages the publication, and in that case the catalog is right there to read.

Hi @arjunQDC, this all would depend on what is set as `publication.autocreate.mode` as you point out.

If the auto-create mode is set to `filtered`, then any existing table column inclusion will be reset back to all columns, and that's the concern. It wouldn't work as someone might expect. I think as long as we document that if you want to use column inclusion, it's the user's responsibility to set up the publication manually, then auto-create mode must inherently be `disabled`. Then it's just a matter of the mapping in the decoder, as you point out.

To @jpechane 's point, later on based on feedback, we can come back and integrate `filtered` with column inclusion/exclusion if there is any community demand.
